question: For a curve with an advisory speed of 40 mph and a radius within 401 to 700 feet, what Chevron Alignment sign spacing and placement are indicated?
model_answer: Direct Answer: For an advisory speed of 40 mph (which falls in the 35 to 45 mph row of Table 2C-5) with a curve radius of 401 to 700 feet, the typical Chevron Alignment (W1-8) sign spacing is 120 feet, measured from the point of curvature (PC). If used, the chevrons must be installed on the outside of the curve, facing approaching traffic at approximately a right angle, at a minimum mounting height of 4 feet. Standards (mandatory): - "If used, Chevron Alignment signs shall be installed on the outside of a turn or curve, in line with and at approximately a right angle to approaching traffic. Chevron Alignment signs shall be installed at a minimum height of 4 feet, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the traveled way." Guidance (recommended): - "The approximate spacing of Chevron Alignment signs on the turn or curve measured from the point of curvature (PC) should be as shown in Table 2C-5." For an advisory speed of 35 to 45 mph and a curve radius of 401 to 700 feet, Table 2C-5 indicates a sign spacing of 120 feet. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Table 2C-5 shows the row "35 to 45 mph / 401 to 700 feet / 120 feet," which covers a 40-mph advisory speed, and notes that the radius–speed relationship in the table should not be used to determine the advisory speed. - [Image 2] Figure 2C-2 (A – Curve) illustrates W1-8L and W1-8R Chevron Alignment signs placed along the outside of the curve for each direction of travel, with a note referring to Table 2C-5 for W1-8 spacing. - [Image 3] Page 199 shows the full Section 2C.08 text, including the Standard for outside-of-curve placement and minimum 4-foot mounting height and the Guidance referencing Table 2C-5 spacing. - [Image 4] Page 197 shows Figure 2C-2 (Sheet 1 of 2) with chevrons arrayed along the outside of the curve in both travel directions. - [Image 5] Page 195 shows Section 2C.05/2C.06 context listing Chevron Alignment (W1-8) signs among treatments for changes in horizontal alignment. - [Image 6] Page 660 (Figure 3G-1) shows delineator placement on a curve and notes that Chevron Alignment signs (W1-8) may be used instead of or in addition to standard delineators. Citations: - Section 2C.08 Standard §4 (p.158) - Section 2C.08 Guidance §5 (p.158) - Table 2C-5 (p.158) - Figure 2C-2 (p.156) - Page 199 - Page 197
gold_answer: Typical spacing is 120 feet. The signs must be on the outside of the curve, approximately at right angles to approaching traffic, with a minimum mounting height of 4 feet.
